nodes.Name: unsafe
nodes.DocComment: for linkname

nodes.Name: Equal
nodes.DocComment:
Equal reports whether a and b
are the same length and contain the same bytes.
A nil argument is equivalent to an empty slice.

nodes.Name: Compare
nodes.DocComment:
Compare returns an integer comparing two byte slices lexicographically.
The result will be 0 if a == b, -1 if a < b, and +1 if a > b.
A nil argument is equivalent to an empty slice.

nodes.Name: explode
nodes.DocComment:
explode splits s into a slice of UTF-8 sequences, one per Unicode code point (still slices of bytes),
up to a maximum of n byte slices. Invalid UTF-8 sequences are chopped into individual bytes.

nodes.Name: Count
nodes.DocComment:
Count counts the number of non-overlapping instances of sep in s.
If sep is an empty slice, Count returns 1 + the number of UTF-8-encoded code points in s.

nodes.Name: Contains
nodes.DocComment: Contains reports whether subslice is within b.

nodes.Name: ContainsAny
nodes.DocComment: ContainsAny reports whether any of the UTF-8-encoded code points in chars are within b.

nodes.Name: ContainsRune
nodes.DocComment: ContainsRune reports whether the rune is contained in the UTF-8-encoded byte slice b.

nodes.Name: ContainsFunc
nodes.DocComment: ContainsFunc reports whether any of the UTF-8-encoded code points r within b satisfy f(r).

nodes.Name: IndexByte
nodes.DocComment: IndexByte returns the index of the first instance of c in b, or -1 if c is not present in b.

nodes.Name: LastIndex
nodes.DocComment: LastIndex returns the index of the last instance of sep in s, or -1 if sep is not present in s.

nodes.Name: LastIndexByte
nodes.DocComment: LastIndexByte returns the index of the last instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

nodes.Name: IndexRune
nodes.DocComment:
IndexRune interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.
It returns the byte index of the first occurrence in s of the given rune.
It returns -1 if rune is not present in s.
If r is [utf8.RuneError], it returns the first instance of any
invalid UTF-8 byte sequence.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: (haveFastIndex && fails > bytealg.Cutover(i)) && i < len(s) || (!haveFastIndex && fails >= 4+i>>4 && i < len(s))

nodes.Name: IndexAny
nodes.DocComment:
IndexAny interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded Unicode code points.
It returns the byte index of the first occurrence in s of any of the Unicode
code points in chars. It returns -1 if chars is empty or if there is no code
point in common.

nodes.Name: LastIndexAny
nodes.DocComment:
LastIndexAny interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded Unicode code
points. It returns the byte index of the last occurrence in s of any of
the Unicode code points in chars. It returns -1 if chars is empty or if
there is no code point in common.

nodes.Name: genSplit
nodes.DocComment:
Generic split: splits after each instance of sep,
including sepSave bytes of sep in the subslices.

nodes.Name: SplitN
nodes.DocComment:
SplitN slices s into subslices separated by sep and returns a slice of
the subslices between those separators.
If sep is empty, SplitN splits after each UTF-8 sequence.
The count determines the number of subslices to return:
  - n > 0: at most n subslices; the last subslice will be the unsplit remainder;
  - n == 0: the result is nil (zero subslices);
  - n < 0: all subslices.

To split around the first instance of a separator, see [Cut].

nodes.Name: SplitAfterN
nodes.DocComment:
SplitAfterN slices s into subslices after each instance of sep and
returns a slice of those subslices.
If sep is empty, SplitAfterN splits after each UTF-8 sequence.
The count determines the number of subslices to return:
  - n > 0: at most n subslices; the last subslice will be the unsplit remainder;
  - n == 0: the result is nil (zero subslices);
  - n < 0: all subslices.

nodes.Name: Split
nodes.DocComment:
Split slices s into all subslices separated by sep and returns a slice of
the subslices between those separators.
If sep is empty, Split splits after each UTF-8 sequence.
It is equivalent to SplitN with a count of -1.

To split around the first instance of a separator, see [Cut].

nodes.Name: SplitAfter
nodes.DocComment:
SplitAfter slices s into all subslices after each instance of sep and
returns a slice of those subslices.
If sep is empty, SplitAfter splits after each UTF-8 sequence.
It is equivalent to SplitAfterN with a count of -1.

nodes.Name: Fields
nodes.DocComment:
Fields interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.
It splits the slice s around each instance of one or more consecutive white space
characters, as defined by [unicode.IsSpace], returning a slice of subslices of s or an
empty slice if s contains only white space. Every element of the returned slice is
non-empty. Unlike [Split], leading and trailing runs of white space characters
are discarded.

nodes.Name: FieldsFunc
nodes.DocComment:
FieldsFunc interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.
It splits the slice s at each run of code points c satisfying f(c) and
returns a slice of subslices of s. If all code points in s satisfy f(c), or
len(s) == 0, an empty slice is returned. Every element of the returned slice is
non-empty. Unlike [Split], leading and trailing runs of code points
satisfying f(c) are discarded.

FieldsFunc makes no guarantees about the order in which it calls f(c)
and assumes that f always returns the same value for a given c.

nodes.Name: Join
nodes.DocComment:
Join concatenates the elements of s to create a new byte slice. The separator
sep is placed between elements in the resulting slice.

nodes.Name: HasPrefix
nodes.DocComment: HasPrefix reports whether the byte slice s begins with prefix.

nodes.Name: HasSuffix
nodes.DocComment: HasSuffix reports whether the byte slice s ends with suffix.

nodes.Name: Map
nodes.DocComment:
Map returns a copy of the byte slice s with all its characters modified
according to the mapping function. If mapping returns a negative value, the character is
dropped from the byte slice with no replacement. The characters in s and the
output are interpreted as UTF-8-encoded code points.

nodes.Name: Repeat
nodes.DocComment:
Repeat returns a new byte slice consisting of count copies of b.

It panics if count is negative or if the result of (len(b) * count)
overflows.

nodes.Name: ToUpper
nodes.DocComment:
ToUpper returns a copy of the byte slice s with all Unicode letters mapped to
their upper case.

nodes.Name: ToLower
nodes.DocComment:
ToLower returns a copy of the byte slice s with all Unicode letters mapped to
their lower case.

nodes.Name: ToTitle
nodes.DocComment: ToTitle treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their title case.

nodes.Name: ToUpperSpecial
nodes.DocComment:
ToUpperSpecial treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their
upper case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

nodes.Name: ToLowerSpecial
nodes.DocComment:
ToLowerSpecial treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their
lower case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

nodes.Name: ToTitleSpecial
nodes.DocComment:
ToTitleSpecial treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all the Unicode letters mapped to their
title case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

nodes.Name: ToValidUTF8
nodes.DocComment:
ToValidUTF8 treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with each run of bytes
representing invalid UTF-8 replaced with the bytes in replacement, which may be empty.

nodes.Name: isSeparator
nodes.DocComment:
isSeparator reports whether the rune could mark a word boundary.
TODO: update when package unicode captures more of the properties.

nodes.Name: Title
nodes.DocComment:
Title treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a copy with all Unicode letters that begin
words mapped to their title case.

Deprecated: The rule Title uses for word boundaries does not handle Unicode
punctuation properly. Use golang.org/x/text/cases instead.

nodes.Name: TrimLeftFunc
nodes.DocComment:
TrimLeftFunc treats s as UTF-8-encoded bytes and returns a subslice of s by slicing off
all leading UTF-8-encoded code points c that satisfy f(c).

nodes.Name: TrimRightFunc
nodes.DocComment:
TrimRightFunc returns a subslice of s by slicing off all trailing
UTF-8-encoded code points c that satisfy f(c).

nodes.Name: TrimFunc
nodes.DocComment:
TrimFunc returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading and trailing
UTF-8-encoded code points c that satisfy f(c).

nodes.Name: TrimPrefix
nodes.DocComment:
TrimPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string.
If s doesn't start with prefix, s is returned unchanged.

nodes.Name: TrimSuffix
nodes.DocComment:
TrimSuffix returns s without the provided trailing suffix string.
If s doesn't end with suffix, s is returned unchanged.

nodes.Name: IndexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
IndexFunc interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.
It returns the byte index in s of the first Unicode
code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

nodes.Name: LastIndexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
LastIndexFunc interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.
It returns the byte index in s of the last Unicode
code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

nodes.Name: indexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
indexFunc is the same as IndexFunc except that if
truth==false, the sense of the predicate function is
inverted.

nodes.Name: lastIndexFunc
nodes.DocComment:
lastIndexFunc is the same as LastIndexFunc except that if
truth==false, the sense of the predicate function is
inverted.

nodes.Name: asciiSet
nodes.DocComment:
asciiSet is a 32-byte value, where each bit represents the presence of a
given ASCII character in the set. The 128-bits of the lower 16 bytes,
starting with the least-significant bit of the lowest word to the
most-significant bit of the highest word, map to the full range of all
128 ASCII characters. The 128-bits of the upper 16 bytes will be zeroed,
ensuring that any non-ASCII character will be reported as not in the set.
This allocates a total of 32 bytes even though the upper half
is unused to avoid bounds checks in asciiSet.contains.

nodes.Name: makeASCIISet
nodes.DocComment:
makeASCIISet creates a set of ASCII characters and reports whether all
characters in chars are ASCII.

nodes.Name: contains
nodes.DocComment: contains reports whether c is inside the set.

nodes.Name: containsRune
nodes.DocComment:
containsRune is a simplified version of strings.ContainsRune
to avoid importing the strings package.
We avoid bytes.ContainsRune to avoid allocating a temporary copy of s.

nodes.Name: Trim
nodes.DocComment:
Trim returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading and
trailing UTF-8-encoded code points contained in cutset.

nodes.Name: TrimLeft
nodes.DocComment:
TrimLeft returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading
UTF-8-encoded code points contained in cutset.

nodes.Name: TrimRight
nodes.DocComment:
TrimRight returns a subslice of s by slicing off all trailing
UTF-8-encoded code points that are contained in cutset.

nodes.Name: TrimSpace
nodes.DocComment:
TrimSpace returns a subslice of s by slicing off all leading and
trailing white space, as defined by Unicode.

nodes.Name: Runes
nodes.DocComment:
Runes interprets s as a sequence of UTF-8-encoded code points.
It returns a slice of runes (Unicode code points) equivalent to s.

nodes.Name: Replace
nodes.DocComment:
Replace returns a copy of the slice s with the first n
non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.
If old is empty, it matches at the beginning of the slice
and after each UTF-8 sequence, yielding up to k+1 replacements
for a k-rune slice.
If n < 0, there is no limit on the number of replacements.

nodes.Name: ReplaceAll
nodes.DocComment:
ReplaceAll returns a copy of the slice s with all
non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new.
If old is empty, it matches at the beginning of the slice
and after each UTF-8 sequence, yielding up to k+1 replacements
for a k-rune slice.

nodes.Name: EqualFold
nodes.DocComment:
EqualFold reports whether s and t, interpreted as UTF-8 strings,
are equal under simple Unicode case-folding, which is a more general
form of case-insensitivity.

nodes.Name: Index
nodes.DocComment: Index returns the index of the first instance of sep in s, or -1 if sep is not present in s.

nodes.Name: Cut
nodes.DocComment:
Cut slices s around the first instance of sep,
returning the text before and after sep.
The found result reports whether sep appears in s.
If sep does not appear in s, cut returns s, nil, false.

Cut returns slices of the original slice s, not copies.

nodes.Name: Clone
nodes.DocComment:
Clone returns a copy of b[:len(b)].
The result may have additional unused capacity.
Clone(nil) returns nil.

nodes.Name: CutPrefix
nodes.DocComment:
CutPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix byte slice
and reports whether it found the prefix.
If s doesn't start with prefix, CutPrefix returns s, false.
If prefix is the empty byte slice, CutPrefix returns s, true.

CutPrefix returns slices of the original slice s, not copies.

nodes.Name: CutSuffix
nodes.DocComment:
CutSuffix returns s without the provided ending suffix byte slice
and reports whether it found the suffix.
If s doesn't end with suffix, CutSuffix returns s, false.
If suffix is the empty byte slice, CutSuffix returns s, true.

CutSuffix returns slices of the original slice s, not copies.
